Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.

spec.name: Spitfire Cyanotype Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I fighter standing on its main wheels and tailwheel, rendered as a cyanotype blueprint: every surface in Prussian-blue tones with white drafting linework, rivets and panel lines as small parts.
spec.layout:
Real Spitfire Mk I size (about 11.2 m span, 9.1 m long) in a three-point ground stance. Fuselage axis is horizontal at y=1.75, nose toward +Z. From front to back: three-blade propeller disc at z=4.0 (radius 1.6, tips clear the floor by 0.15 m), a white-tipped spinner, a round Merlin cowl with 6 fishtail exhaust stacks per side, the long slim fuselage, a framed bubble canopy at z -1.7..1.0, a turtleback fairing, then the tail cone carrying a tall rounded fin and elliptical tailplane. Low elliptical wings (dihedral about 6 degrees, root y=1.22 rising to y=1.62 at the tips) with a straight leading edge and a curved trailing edge. They carry an oil cooler under the left wing (+X) and a radiator under the right wing (-X), four gun barrels in each leading edge, and ailerons and flaps. Main gear legs splay outward to wheels at x=+-1.4, z=0.6; the tailwheel sits at z=-4.05. Nothing else is on the floor and there is no ground plane.

STYLE: everything is cyanotype blue. Underside = light sky blue (skyPale/sky), top and side skin = cobalt with disruptive camouflage patches of prussian, darker shadow zones in navy, deepest ink for tyres, exhaust, gaps and recesses. Linework is WHITE and pale: panel lines, rib lines, stringers, rivet rows, control-surface hinge lines and bright edge trim along leading edges and tips are thin small parts seated on the surface, so the plane reads as white drafting lines on blue paper. Roundels are concentric flat discs (outer navy ring, pale ring, sky ring, white centre); the fin flash is three vertical bands (sky, white, navy). Details are fine and fussy; the silhouette stays simple, blocky and bold. Glowing cyan (cyanGlow, via the glow kit) is used only for the gunsight reflector and the wingtip and tail lights. Colour by place: lighter on top, darker below, soot at the exhausts, a pale chipped strip on the wing-root walkway.

parts.builds: The whole fuselage skin and its surface detail, from the cowl to the tail-cone end. Loft stations (z, half-width, top y, bottom y): z3.95 cowl ring r~0.5 centred y1.75; z3.0 hw0.52 top2.3 bot1.22; z1.5 hw0.55 top2.28 bot1.12; z0.5 hw0.55 top2.1 bot1.1; z-1.0 hw0.5 top2.1 bot1.2; z-1.7 hw0.42 top2.05; z-3.0 hw0.25 top1.95 bot1.45; z-4.45 hw0.06 top1.82 bot1.6. The upper deck is flat at y=2.1 from z=-1.7 to z=1.0 so the cockpit part sits on it (the cockpit rises from the sill at y=2.0..2.1). A turtleback fairing sits behind the canopy (z-1.7..-2.8) and slopes down into the tail cone. Colours: upper half cobalt with prussian disruptive patches, lower half skyPale with a wavy demarcation line in white, a navy chin under the nose. Details: cowl nose ring plus cowl panel seam bands and ~16 white cowl fastener dots in rings; 6 fishtail exhaust stacks on each side of the cowl at z 2.4..3.3 (ink pipes with navy soot streaks behind them); small bulged cannon-blister bumps; oil-tank carb scoop under the nose at z 2.0..2.8 (navy frame, ink opening); aerial mast (white rod with a pale tip) at z=1.7 on the top deck, up to y 2.7, with a wire sweeping back to the tail (thin white sweep); white panel lines, access hatches, stringers and rivet rows along the sides; two roundels on the fuselage sides at z=-2.3 (outer navy, pale, sky, white centre discs seated on the surface, x=+-0.3 surface); blocky white serial and squadron code letters (e.g. 'QJ' and 'K', built as box strokes) either side of the roundel; a wing-root fairing strip (pale walkway) where the wings join (z -0.9..0.7, y about 1.2); a spine light on the tail cone top. No propeller, wings, cockpit glazing or tail surfaces.
parts.attaches: Cowl front meets the spinner at mount cowlFront; deck meets the cockpit at deckTop, windscreenBase and canopyRear; wing roots enter at wingRootL and wingRootR (wing roots are buried inside the fuselage sides); tail cone end meets the fin and tailplane at tailBase.

parts.builds: The cockpit and canopy, on top of the fuselage deck. A sliding-hood bubble canopy shown as a white frame structure (curved hoops, a longitudinal rail, a bottom sill rail, a rear glazing frame), the side panes left open as a framework (blueprint skeleton) with only thin pale glass panes (glass colour) inside the windscreen: a bulletproof flat centre panel and two raked side panels, white frame bars. The canopy rides the canopy joint and the windscreen the body joint. Inside: a bucket seat (prussian, with pale cushion), an armour plate and headrest behind it, a pilot bust (navy flying suit, skyPale face, dark goggles, ink helmet with white strap, an arm to the stick), a control stick with a ring grip, a rudder pedal pair, an instrument panel with round gauge discs (a few as textured dials from white rings and tick marks, or built from small ring parts) and a white edge, a gunsight with a glowing cyanGlow reflector glass, a rear-view mirror on the hood top and a sliding-hood handle. A thin white outline sweep traces the canopy edge for the drafting look.
parts.attaches: Sits on the fuselage deck, between windscreenBase (front) and canopyRear (back), at deckTop height y=2.1; frames sink slightly into the sill.

parts.builds: Both elliptical wings as mirrored builds, left (+X) and right (-X). Planform: leading edge runs from (0.5,1.3,1.2) at the root to (5.6,1.65,0.3) at the tip; trailing edge from (0.5,1.15,-1.4) to (5.6,1.6,-0.25) with an elliptical bulge (about z -0.95 at x=3). Root thickness 0.3 tapering to 0.08 at the tip, dihedral about 6 degrees (root y1.22, tip y1.62). Built as lofted or extruded slab with a rounded leading edge; upper surface cobalt with prussian camouflage patches, underside skyPale. Ailerons on the outer trailing edge (x 3.0..5.1) ride the aileronL and aileronR joints; flaps on the inner trailing edge (x 0.9..2.9) are shown in sky with white hinge lines. Details: white rib lines across the wing at regular spacing, rivet rows, a pale leading edge trim, a pale wing-root walkway panel, an upper-surface roundel at x=+-3.3, z=-0.1 (concentric discs navy, pale, sky, white) and an underside roundel, an oil cooler scoop under the left wing at x=2.2 (round-ish, steel with an ink opening) and a rectangular radiator under the right wing at x=-2.2 (blue box with a white outline and an ink intake), four .303 gun barrels per wing at x=+-1.7, +-1.95, +-2.2 and +-2.45 poking 0.12 m ahead of the leading edge (gunmetal tubes with ink muzzle holes and pale taped ports), a pitot tube on the left leading edge at x=3.6, cannon bulge fairings on the upper surface, navigation lights at the tips (glowing cyanGlow), and a tip trim cap in white. No landing gear.
parts.attaches: Roots are buried in the fuselage sides at wingRootL and wingRootR; wing tips end at wingTipL and wingTipR; gear hips pass through the underside at gearHipL and gearHipR (gear part owns the leg and doors); ailerons hinge at aileronHingeL and aileronHingeR.

parts.builds: The whole empennage and the tailwheel. A tall rounded Spitfire fin extruded from the tail cone up to finTop at y=3.3 (leading edge swept back from z=-3.5 at the base to z=-4.0 at the top), with the rudder (rides the rudder joint, a hinged rib-lined panel with a balance horn and a trim tab, white rib lines) behind it. The fin flash is three vertical bands (sky, white, navy) on both sides of the fin leading edge. An elliptical tailplane (span 3.2, root chord 1.0, centred at tailplaneCenter) with elevators (ride elevatorL and elevatorR, with trim tabs and white rib lines) on the trailing edge; upper surface cobalt, underside skyPale, white hinge lines, rivet rows and pale edge trim. A fin-root fillet blends fin and tail cone. Tailwheel assembly on the tailwheel joint: a short oleo strut from tailwheelHip (0,1.5,-3.9) to tailwheelAxle (0,0.12,-4.05), a fork, an ink tyre of radius 0.12 with a pale hub that touches y=0, and a small fairing. A rear navigation light on the fin trailing edge in cyanGlow, and white drafting trim along the fin leading edge.
parts.attaches: Fin and tailplane roots sink into the tail cone at tailBase; the tailplane is centred on tailplaneCenter; the rudder hinges at rudderHinge; the strut starts at tailwheelHip under the tail cone and the wheel rests at tailwheelAxle with the floor at y=0.

parts.builds: The propeller group and the main undercarriage. Propeller on the prop joint at propHub (0,1.75,4.0): a spun spinner (lathe, 0.7 m long from z 3.95 to 4.65, prussian with a white band and a pale tip) with a ring of pale bolt dots, a back plate, a hub with a blade-root cuff on each blade, and three wide blades of radius 1.6 at 120 degrees apart (one pointing straight up), each with a pitch twist, a leading edge in white trim, blade body navy to prussian, a pale tip band at the outer 0.2 m and a stencilled white line near the root. Main gear: for each side a leg on legL and legR from the gear hip (+-1.0,1.12,0.5) to the wheel axle (+-1.4,0.34,0.6): a chunky oleo strut (steel, pale chrome collar, navy scissor link), a leg fairing door (extruded D-shape, cobalt with white edge lines and rivets) hanging outboard, and a wheel on the wheelL and wheelR joints (ink tyre, radius 0.34, width 0.18, a chunky tread ring in navy, a pale hub disc with 5 spoke or bolt dots, axle cap) with a bearing axle stub and a small wheel-well flap on the underside skin. The lowest points of the wheels rest at y=0 (centres at y=0.34), and the propeller tips clear the floor by 0.15 m.
parts.attaches: The spinner back plate meets the cowl at cowlFront and the hub spins about propHub; leg tops sink into the wing underside at gearHipL and gearHipR; wheels centre on wheelAxleL and wheelAxleR. This box overlaps the fuselage and wing boxes in x and z, but the geometry stays in the propeller disc and the gear zone (z 0.1..1.0).

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the Spitfire's real-world proportions for a cyanotype blueprint style—roughly 11.2m wingspan, 9.1m length, 3.9m height—and planning a three-point ground stance with the tail wheel down, oriented along +Z.

I'm calculating placement details: the thrust line, propeller clearance, fin and canopy heights, fuselage z-extents from spinner to tail, and main/tail wheel positions. For the overall look, I'm settling on a deep Prussian blue palette with lighter blue accents and white linework to capture that classic cyanotype blueprint aesthetic.

Now I'm planning the part breakdown: fuselage with exhaust stacks and roundels, a cockpit section with canopy, pilot bust, and instruments, then wings with elliptical shape, ailerons, flaps, and under-wing radiators, each assigned rough geometry budgets.

For the remaining pieces, I'm splitting tail and empennage (fin, rudder, tailplane, elevators, tailwheel) with its own joints, and a final section covering the nose spinner, three-blade propeller hub, and landing gear with main legs, wheels, and doors.

Now I'm mapping out joint positions: body as the root spine, a hinge for the propeller at the nose, and wing attachment points for left and right wings branching off the fuselage.

I'm working through the wing planform with an elliptical Spitfire-style shape—root chord around 2.6m tapering to a narrower tip chord near the 5.6m span point, with slight dihedral lifting the tips upward and the leading/trailing edges curving appropriately along the 11.2m total span.

Now I'm placing the pitot tube on the left wing, defining the aileron hinge along the outer trailing edge, positioning the two radiators asymmetrically under each wing (round oil cooler on one side, rectangular on the other), and spacing out the four gun barrels that protrude forward of the leading edge on each wing.

For the tail, I'm setting the fin and tailplane positions near the rear fuselage, adding rudder and elevator hinge joints, and sketching out the main gear leg attachment points on the fuselage, leaving the tailwheel as a simple static part.

Now I'm working out the Spitfire's distinctive raked main gear geometry—legs mounted on the wing angling outward and forward so the wheels sit ahead of the center of mass, with joints defining the leg pivot and wheel attachment points.

I also need to place the tailwheel, attached via a short strut from the fuselage bottom near the tail, with a hinge joint so it can be included as a leg-like part. Then I'm checking that the wheel radii are sized correctly (around 0.34m, matching the real Spitfire's wheel diameter) so the lowest points of the gear touch the ground plane properly.

Next I'm working through the fuselage silhouette: cowl radius near the nose, the wider cockpit section with canopy height, and the gradual taper toward the tail, while marking which parts (gear, tailwheel) should register as floor-contact and which (radiators, wings) shouldn't.

Setting overall dimensions now: keeping the fuselage axis roughly horizontal with a slight tail rise, then computing total size from wingspan, fin height, and nose-to-tail length to define the bounding box before I start laying out the individual part boxes.

Working out the fuselage box with separate attachment points for the tail cone, fin, and tailplane, plus a tail box that includes the tailwheel and sits flush with the floor.

For the cockpit I'm thinking through a bubble-canopy approach: since solid fuselage primitives can't have real cutouts, I want the canopy rendered as a wireframe of frame bars rather than solid glass panels, so the seat and pilot read through underneath like a blueprint sketch, with the windscreen as a lighter panel up front.

I'm placing the cockpit deck at y=2.05-2.1, fairing the nose and sill heights into a slight hump near the cowl, and sizing the cockpit box roughly from z=-1.75 to 1.0 so the tail fairs in cleanly behind the canopy.

For the wings, I'm bounding them from x=-5.6 to 5.6 and z=-1.4 to 1.5, keeping gun positions near the leading edge and dropping the radiator slightly below the wing underside, while leaving gear wells and doors to the separate landing gear component.

Now I'm figuring out where the wing roots mount into the fuselage, placing them symmetrically at x=±0.55, y≈1.2-1.22, with the chord centered around z=-0.1, and working out the dihedral so the wingtip rises from root height 1.22 up to about 1.6-1.7.

I'm sketching the wing's leading and trailing edges from root to tip, with a curved elliptical bulge along the trailing edge, then turning to the prop and landing gear boxes, noticing their z-ranges overlap and considering consolidating them into a single part or reorganizing the nose prop section.

I'll settle on a five-part breakdown with rough detail budgets: fuselage (skin, cowl, exhaust, tail cone, markings), cockpit (canopy, seat, pilot, instruments), wings (both sides, ailerons, flaps, radiators, guns, lights), tail group (fin, rudder, tailplane, elevators, tailwheel), and propeller plus undercarriage together.

For the propeller/undercarriage bounding box, I'm working out the geometry so the prop disc and spinner fit properly relative to the fin height, settling on a box that slightly overlaps the wing and fuselage regions, which I'll note as acceptable.

Now I'm picking a blueprint-style color palette limited to flat blues and whites, capped at 24 colors—navy ink, deep prussian hull, main cyan blue skin, lighter highlight blue for top surfaces, and a sky tone.

Continuing the palette, I'm working out roundel rings in pale, navy, and white, plus a darker soot tone for exhaust panels, dark blue prop blades with light tip bands, navy wheels with pale hubs, and a glowing cyan accent for nav lights and the gunsight reticle.

I'm skipping serial text and dimension lines, maybe leaving space for simple blocky fuselage code letters like "QJ-K" for the fuselage builder to add later, and deciding against including any ground grid. Now I'm defining key mount points on the airframe—thrust line, cowl front, prop hub, deck top, windscreen base, canopy rear, and wing root—each as specific coordinate positions.

I continue plotting out wing tip, gear hip, wheel axle, tail base, fin top, tailplane, and tailwheel axle positions, noting that exhaust stacks belong to the fuselage and radiators belong to the wings. Then I start sketching the joint hierarchy, with the body as the root spine and the propeller parented to the body at the nose, assigning it a fan role.

Now I'm defining the wing joints with left and right orientations, then placing the aileron hinges by interpolating the trailing edge position along the wing span and offsetting the hinge forward of the curved trailing edge for proper chord placement.

Now I'm working through the landing gear hierarchy, parenting legL to the wing with a computed hinge direction toward the wheel, and sketching the tailwheel strut position near the tail, deciding to skip spin hinges for simplicity.

I'm adding the canopy as a sliding hinge joint parented to the body, with cockpit geometry riding both canopy and body joints. I'm also tallying part mass budgets to confirm they stay under the 900 limit before moving on to writing the detailed layout spec.

For the visual style, I'm working out the cyanotype color scheme: dark navy for undersides, brighter cobalt blues for top surfaces, with white linework marking panel lines, rivets, and stringers. I'm translating the classic Spitfire camouflage pattern (dark green/earth top, sky-blue underside) into this blue-and-white cyanotype palette, using pale sky-blue tones for the belly and deeper cobalt patches for the disruptive top camo.

Now I'm mapping out the roundel placements on fuselage sides and wing surfaces, assigning ownership so the fuselage builder handles fuselage roundels and codes, the wing builder handles wing roundels, and the tail builder handles the fin flash stripes. I'm also laying out the fuselage cross-section stations, starting with the cowl front ring dimensions and vertical positioning at the nose.

I'm continuing the loft stations down the fuselage from the chin/radiator area through the sill, the hump, and into the turtleback fairing, tapering toward the tail. Next I'm planning the exhaust stacks, six per side.

I'm fleshing out the pilot figure with helmet, goggles, torso and arm on the stick, plus cockpit details like the instrument panel, glowing gunsight, rear-view mirror, and headrest armor plate. I'm debating exact placement of the antenna mast relative to the canopy, trying to recall whether it sits ahead of or behind the windscreen on a real Spitfire.

Now I'm settling the mast position on the fuselage top and moving on to the propeller assembly -- three blades with twisted pitch spaced 120 degrees apart, a banded lathe-turned spinner, root cuffs, and tip bands, with one blade resting straight up. I'm also planning the landing gear with oleo struts, scissor links, tread-patterned tires, spoked hubs, and D-shaped fairing doors in blueprint blue with white edge lines.

I'm now adding the tail assembly: fin and rudder with rib lines, an elliptical tailplane with elevators and trim tabs, a tailwheel with strut, a tri-band fin flash, a glowing tip position light, and a fillet where the tail cone meets the fuselage. Writing the fuselage box coordinates and exhaust stack placement...

Defining more bounding boxes...

I'm picking a limited color palette—deep inks, navys, cobalts, sky tones, and metallic accents—then writing out the mounts, joints, and parts with concise but descriptive details, keeping in mind there's no ground plane in this scene.

I'm planning the wing-building function, working out joint placement for the root and aileron on each side, and considering how to loft the wing geometry across stations along its length.

Instead, I'll construct separate upper and lower surface meshes directly, computing leading/trailing edge curves and dihedral along the span, then shaping an airfoil thickness profile at each chord position.

Still writing airfoil code...

Adding wing details now: aileron patches, camo panels, and rib lines swept along the chord using curved point paths. I'll skip individual rivets for performance and instead approximate rivet rows with thin dashed sweeps.

Setting up bones for mirrored wing geometry, then adding gun barrels, muzzle discs, an oil cooler cylinder under the wing, and a radiator box with framed outline before moving to the pitot tube.

Pitot rod placement, nav light glow sphere, tip cap, cannon bulges, and a white leading-edge trim sweep, plus a pale walkway patch on the wing surface. Now I'm writing the patch-building function that generates grid positions, indices, and bone-flat-colored geometry, making sure the winding order keeps upper faces oriented correctly.

I'm working out the normal-flip logic for the grid mesh — building a helper that generates points, computes the first triangle's normal, and flips winding if it doesn't face outward based on the side sign. I'm also refining the leading and trailing edge z-coordinate interpolation functions to shape the elliptical wing profile smoothly from root to tip.

Now I'm defining the chord position, thickness, and y-coordinate functions for the wing surface points, making sure the root and thickness values stay within bounds. I'm setting up the span-wise and chord-wise station grids for the upper and lower wing skins, using a power curve to cluster points near the leading edge, and planning how to handle the tip cap closure.

The leading edge needs upper and lower surfaces meeting at the same point at u=0, and the trailing edge needs them converging at u=1 where thickness goes to zero, so the surface stays properly closed. Time to write the code now.
